record.title: VLM-in-Sandbox reports bounded visual evidence state for multimodal agents
record.summary: The preprint presents a training-free visual workspace that registers sandbox-generated images in a ledger, keeps active visual context bounded and lets the model choose which artifacts to re-inspect. Across seven benchmarks, the authors report a 2.52 percentage-point pooled accuracy gain for GPT-4.1-mini over an append-only sandbox on 6,350 examples (95% CI 1.83–3.21), with 302 rescues and 142 regressions. A compiler-matched study on 1,260 examples reports 66.27% accuracy with 18.6% fewer total tokens than an automatic retain-all control. These are author-reported results, with heterogeneous per-benchmark effects and no independent reproduction.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: VLM-in-Sandbox stores generated visual artifacts in an addressable ledger and uses model-directed promotion with a bounded active visual context.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports a 2.52 percentage-point pooled accuracy gain over Original Append-only on 6,350 GPT-4.1-mini examples, alongside 302 rescues and 142 regressions.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The author-reported benchmark results do not establish independent reproducibility or universal accuracy, compute or latency gains across multimodal agent deployments.

evidence_gaps.description: The benchmark and matched-ablation results have not been independently reproduced.
Total serving cost and transfer across model families are not established by the reported token savings.

brief.importance_rationale: If explicit, bounded visual evidence state reliably improves multimodal agent accuracy while reducing repeated visual-context cost, it would change how tool-enabled VLM systems manage images and intermediate artifacts. The paper reports broad but author-run benchmark gains with mixed per-task outcomes; independent replication and deployment cost remain open.
limitations: All empirical results are paper-reported; the research desk did not run code or independently reproduce them.
The primary GPT-4.1-mini comparison reports both 302 rescues and 142 regressions; results vary materially by benchmark.
The 1,260-example matched ablation changes visual visibility and retention controls; it does not establish that token reduction alone causes the accuracy result.
A training-free system depends on the base VLM to decide when to use tools and which visual evidence to revisit.
Fewer visual tokens do not by themselves establish lower total inference compute or deployment cost.

technical.claimed_result: On seven benchmarks and 6,350 examples, the paper reports GPT-4.1-mini pooled accuracy +2.52 pp versus Original Append-only (95% CI 1.83–3.21; 302 rescues, 142 regressions). In a compiler-matched 2×2 study on 1,260 examples, it reports 66.27% accuracy with 18.6% fewer total tokens than the automatic retain-all control. Results vary by benchmark; some individual confidence intervals include zero.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv v1 paper reports the method, benchmark setup, paired analyses and results. the research desk did not run code or independently reproduce any result; outcomes remain author-reported.
technical.mechanism: A sandbox tool generates visual artifacts and records them with stable identifiers and provenance in an image ledger. The model can inspect selected artifacts, promote evidence for later context, and operate with bounded active visual slots; this separates artifact generation from evidence management.
technical.regime: Seven multimodal benchmarks, four base VLMs in the paper's broader evaluation, with the primary paired comparison using GPT-4.1-mini versus Original Append-only across 6,350 examples. A compiler-matched ablation uses 1,260 examples. A separate local vLLM systems study reports request and latency measures.
technical.strongest_baseline: Original Append-only for the primary GPT-4.1-mini comparison; the matched 2×2 study compares model-directed visibility and bounded retention against an automatic retain-all control.

brief.title: VLM-in-Sandbox reports bounded visual evidence state for multimodal agents
brief.why_it_matters: Multimodal agents can accumulate crops, masks and rendered analyses faster than they can fit them into the active context. An explicit evidence ledger and selective re-entry policy are a concrete alternative to either discarding artifacts or appending all of them indefinitely. The reported gains are modest in aggregate and include regressions, so the result supports testing the design rather than assuming universal benefit.
